images.title: A tray of halwa
images.purpose: Set up the question: a tray cut into 6 equal pieces with 2 shaded, so the child looks for other fractions that shade the same part.
images.composition: One long flat tray centred with wide white space, its fraction above it, and one cue line below.
images.exact_structure: One flat rectangular tray seen from above, outlined dark, cut by 5 straight lines into 6 equal pieces in a single row. The left 2 pieces are filled amber #E69F00; the other 4 pieces are plain. A teal #0072B2 fraction sits above the tray. Below the tray, one cue line in reddish purple #CC79A7 and one question line in dark text. No other cuts, no spoon, no plate. Exactly 1 tray, 6 equal pieces, 2 amber pieces.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
the fractions 1/3, 3/9 or 4/12 anywhere in the frame, or extra cuts in the tray
images.takeaway: Divide or multiply the top and the bottom of 2/6 by the same number to find equal fractions.
images.description: A halwa tray cut into 6 equal pieces in one row with 2 pieces amber, labelled 2/6, and the cue same number, top and bottom.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to point at the 2 amber pieces and say what number could divide or multiply both 2 and 6.

image_decisions.why: A shaded tray keeps the amount 2/6 in view while the child finds equal fractions, without showing them.
